caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 65 of 1986.
lawyer:
Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Mohammadullah, Giasuddin Ahmed and Mohd. Ismail Gazi, Advocates  ----- For the Appellant. 
Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, Ruhul Amin and Sirajur Rahman, Advocates ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Progati Industries Ltd ----- Appellant
Vs.
Shahida Khatun and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Deceased plaintiff Abdul Halim who died during the pendency of the suit filed Title Suit No. 347 of 1977 in the First Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on 14.9.1977 against defendants for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit property measuring 1.50 acres of land with buildings and structures thereon appertaining to plot  Nos. 151 and 157 of Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka. 

 3. Arc the plaintiffs entitled to a decree for recovery of khas possession of the suit property? 

 6. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record decreed the suit holding that (1) that the suit is maintainable (2) that Title Suit No. 315/1968 filed by the PICIC was decreed on compromise on 18.11.70(3) that the plaintiff entered into an agreement on 29.11.69 with M/s. Rana Tractors and Equipment’s Ltd. to sell the suit property but no possession as per the said agreement was delivered to the said purchaser and the plaintiff was in possession of the Suit property till his dispossession by defendant No. 1 in 1972; (4) that the deceased plaintiff was the absolute owner of the suit property and the defendant No. 1 admitted the ownership and title of the plaintiff in paragraph 7 of the written statement (5) that installments were not paid by M/s. Rana Tractors and Equipment’s Ltd according to the terms of the compromise decree and unless a final decree was passed ownership of the mortgagor was not extinguished and still subsists (6) that the Government did not take over the control and management of the suit property by notification and as such suit properties do not come within the purview of Acting President's Order No. 1/1972 and the suit property is not an abandoned property (7) that since the defendant No. 1 dispossessed the plaintiffs, they are entitled to recover khas possession from the trespasser. 

 8. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff respondents, submitted that the suit as framed for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land against the trespasser M/s. Progati Industries Ltd was not bad for defect of parties inasmuch as the said trespasser and the Government of Bangladesh under the provision of PO 142 of 1972 were the only necessary parties. He further submitted that the deceased plaintiff was admittedly in possession of the suit property upto 29.11.69 when the deed of agreement for sale of the suit property was executed and if time is calculated from that date then the suit was filed within 12 years on 14.9.77 and the suit was not barred by limitation. But the learned counsel found it difficult to support the judgment in the face of the pleadings and the evidence on record. 

 9. We have been led through the pleadings, oral and documentary evidence on record and also the impugned judgment in this appeal. We have considered the arguments from both sides with reference to the pleadings evidence on record and the impugned judgment and decree. We have noticed that the issues were re-cast by the trial Court on 28.6.86 in course of hearing arguments in the suit. No issue regarding defect of parties or limitation was framed by the Trial Court after recasting the issues. The defendant No. 1 in paras 4 and 12 of their written statement raised the question of defect of parties but there is no pleading regarding the suit being barred by limitation. From the pleadings and evidence on record we find that the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession having been filed on 16.9.77 from the alleged date of dispossession in March 1972 was apparently not barred by limitation under Article 142 of the Limitation Act and that is why bar of Limitation was not pleaded by the defendant. The defendant No. 1 is a nationalised company placed under the Bangladesh Engineering and Ship Building Corporation as per Gazettee notification dated 18.3.72 Ext. R(1) and Gazettee notification dated 7.7.72 Ext: R correcting the earlier notification. The said corporation was subsequently renamed as the Bangladesh Steel and Engineering Corporation. The defendant No. 1 has not lost its legal entity as a juristic person and can sue and be said without the said corporation which controls and supervises its activities under the provisions of Bangladesh Industrial Enterprises (Nationalisation) Order 1972 (P 0 No. 27 of 1972) and as such the suit could proceed against the defendant No. 1 without impleading the said corporation. Under the provision of Section 6 of the Bangladesh Transfer of Immovable Property (Temporary Provision;) Order 1972 (PO 142 of 1972) the Government is a necessary party in a suit for declaration of title when directly or indirectly Government is going to be affected and under the provision of section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure "Government is to be represented either by the Deputy Commissioner or by the Secretary of the Government when affairs of the Railways is not involved in the suit. The defendant No. 1 in their written statement has not specifically raised any objection as to the Government defendant No. 2 not being represented by the Secretary of the appropriate Ministry instead of the Deputy Commissioner and as such we are of the view that the suit was not bad for defect of the parties. In this appeal we are to see whether the learned trial Court was justified in holding that the plaintiff had title and possession till he was dispossessed by the defendant No. 1. Admittedly the deceased plaintiff became owner and possessor of the suit property as per deed of agreement for lease dated 25.1.1956 Ext. 1 on payment of Rs. 3,375/- as part of the premium out of total premium of Rs. 27,675/- undertaking to pay the balance Rs. 24,300/- in twenty equal annual instalments and annual rent of Rs. 450/- to the Government. Admittedly the deceased plaintiff entered into written agreement on 29.11.1969 Ext. 4 to sell the suit property to the purchaser company at a consideration of Rs. 3,60,000/- on receipt of Rs. 65,000/- as advance as acknowledged in paragraph 4 of the said agreement as well as by granting a separate receipt dated 29.11.69 Ext. C for Rs. 65,000/00 by two cheques. Delivery of vacant physical possession of the demised suit property to the said purchaser company was as know lodged in paragraph No. 5 of the said agreement. We find from the said agreement that the deceased plaintiff entered into the said agreement to raise money to pay mortgage debt of his M/s. Dacca Wood Works Ltd to the PICIC and the purchaser company agreed to furnish a bank guarantee for Rs. 1,36,000/- in favour of the PICIC who shall redeem the suit mortgage property in favour of the said purchaser company on receipt of the said Bank guarantee and on completion of all the instalments of the Bank guarantee property shall automatically be redeemed in favour of the said purchaser company and all documents shall be returned to the said purchaser company by the PICIC who will also withdraw TS No. 315/1968 from the 1st court of Sub-Judge, Dhaka and that further sum of Rs. 50,000/00 shall be paid by 15th December 1969 and balance sum of Rs 1,09,000/00 will be paid at the time of registration of the sale deed. From the compromise decree dated 18.11.1970 Ext. 3 as well as Ext. "A we find that the said Title Suit was filed on 19.11.68 by the PICIC against M/s. Dacca Wood Works Ltd, deceased plaintiff and other directors of the said company for enforcement of mortgage by deposit of title deeds for realization of Rs. 1,69,952/23 by sale of the mortgaged property and the said purchaser company was added as defendant No. 5 on 12.6.70 and the deceased plaintiff entered into the said agreement on 29.11.89 with the said purchaser company with the permission of the PICIC on condition .of furnishing a bank guarantee for Rs. 1,36,000/- to PICIC in full and final settlement of the loan of M/s. Dacca Wood Works Ltd and that the PICIC received the sum of Tk. 45,333/00 by a pay order dated 12.3.70 from the said purchaser company and encased the same on 2.4.70 and the said purchaser company also furnished a Bank guarantees for Rs. 90,667/00 in favour of the PICIC guaranteeing payment of Rs. 45,333/00 on 31.12.70 and Rs. 45,334/00 on 31.12.71; that on such payments being made the mortgaged suit property shall be redeemed in favour of the said purchaser company and the documents relating to the said properties shall be returned to the said purchaser company but in default of payment of the said instalments the mortgaged suit property shall be sold and the money thus realised shall be applied in payment of the amounts due to the PICIC and balance amount, if any, shall be paid to the said purchaser company. 

 21. We, therefore, hold that neither the deceased plaintiff was nor his successors, the substituted plaintiffs are entitled to declaration of title in the suit property and the substituted plaintiffs are debarred from asserting their title or any right in the suit property not only against the transferee M/s. Rana Tractors and Equipments Ltd. but also against the defendants who; have been possessing the same under the said purchaser company. So Court below was not justified in declaring plaintiffs title in the suit property. The deceased plaintiff having delivered possession of the suit property in part performance of written contract for sale was not entitled to recover khas possession by ejecting the defendants who are in lawful possession of the suit property. We have already found that the substituted plaintiffs have failed to prove alleged possession and, dispossession. The deceased plaintiff came before the court with a false case and the substituted plaintiffs adduced false oral evidence contrary to the documentary evidence so the suit is liable to be dismissed.
